angle: In Simcoe County a hot tub or sauna is four-season equipment: it earns its keep on January nights after the ski hill, on damp April weekends at the lake, and on every evening a Highway 400 commuter finally gets home.

hot-tub.intro: Long winters, deep snow and a cottage an hour up the road shape how people around here buy. Every Jacuzzi, Nordic, Aquasolus and Wellness Shop Ontario tub below is priced exactly as it sits on our Bryne Drive floor.
body: Barrie sits in the snow belt, and the squalls that roll off Georgian Bay can drop a foot overnight on a cover that has to hold it. We recommend a cover lifter on every tub we deliver here, and we help you place the tub so the snow you clear off the deck does not land on the cabinet. A tub running at full temperature through a Simcoe County winter needs real insulation and a tight cover; the difference shows up on your February hydro bill. Right now every new 2026 Jacuzzi in stock is 20% off in our Red Tag inventory clearance, not combinable with other offers.

Lots here range widely. South Barrie, Innisfil and Bradford new builds usually have a tight rear yard, a six foot gate and a basement panel close to the back wall, which makes for a straightforward dolly delivery and a short electrical run. Older homes in Allandale and the east end often have mature trees and a narrower side yard, so we measure before we quote. Cottage and waterfront properties on Lake Simcoe or Georgian Bay are a different job: sloped lots, seasonal roads and long distances to the hydro panel. Our crews handle all of it, including crane lifts over a cottage roof.

Who buys here: families in the subdivisions along Mapleview and Big Bay Point Road who want a seven seat J-385 or J-485 the kids can pile into, commuters who sit in Highway 400 traffic and want the J-335 running when they pull in, and cottage owners who take a Nordic Retreat All-In-110V up north because it plugs into what the cottage already has. Skiers heading home from Horseshoe Valley or Blue Mountain are our January regulars. If your water comes from a well, tell us; we set up water care differently for hard or high iron water than for Barrie municipal supply.

faq.q: Can I run a hot tub at a cottage with only 100 amp service?
faq.a: Usually yes. The Nordic Sport All-In-110V and Retreat All-In-110V plug into a dedicated standard outlet and heat more slowly, which suits a cottage used on weekends. If you want a full 240V Jacuzzi at the lake, have an ESA licensed electrician do a load calculation first; many cottages have room for a 50 amp GFCI circuit once the baseboard heaters are accounted for.

faq.q: When is the best time of year to have a tub delivered to a cottage?
faq.a: Late spring after the half load season lifts, or fall before the seasonal roads close. Spring load restrictions on county and township roads limit what a delivery truck can carry for several weeks, so we schedule around them. Winter deliveries to plowed year round roads are fine and common in Barrie itself.

faq.q: How much snow can a hot tub cover take?
faq.a: The covers on the Jacuzzi and Nordic tubs we sell are built to carry a normal snow load, but a wet Georgian Bay squall can pile on more weight than any cover should sit under for days. Brush it off when it gets deep, the same as you would a gazebo roof. A cover lifter makes that easier and keeps the cover out of the snowbank when you get in.

faq.q: Does well water change how I look after the tub?
faq.a: Yes. Well water in Oro-Medonte, Essa and rural Innisfil often runs hard with iron or manganese, which stains shells and clouds water if you fill straight from the hose. We recommend a pre-filter on the fill hose and a metal sequestering treatment at start-up. On Barrie or Orillia municipal water the routine is simpler, and we will set you up with the right test strips either way.

faq.q: Will the tub stay warm if we lose power in a winter storm?
faq.a: A full foam insulated tub with the cover on holds usable heat for a day or more in a typical outage, and the water will not freeze for considerably longer. For cottages that sit empty, ask us about freeze protection and the SmartTub app on the J-400 and J-500 series so you get a temperature alert on your phone. A small generator can run the circulation pump if outages are common on your road.

swim-spa.intro: A swim spa gives you a lap lane you can use in February, which matters in a region where the outdoor pool season is barely three months and the lake stays cold until July. Every model here is a heated, year round installation.
body: Lake Simcoe and Georgian Bay give this area a lot of swimmers and paddlers, and most of them lose their training water from Thanksgiving to Victoria Day. A swim spa closes that gap. Triathletes and masters swimmers around here use the 19 foot Jacuzzi J-19 PowerPro for its current, families in Innisfil pick the 13 foot J-13 PowerPlay for its eight seats, and retirees who want gentle resistance walking choose the 12 foot J-12 Flow at $30,695. None of them need to drive to a pool at six in the morning through a snow squall.

Winter running cost is the question we hear most from Simcoe County buyers, and it comes down to insulation, cover and placement. Site the spa out of the prevailing west wind if you can, with the long side against a fence or the house, and keep the cover sealed when nobody is in it. The dual temperature models, the Jacuzzi J-19DT PowerPro at $60,895 and the SwimLife SwimExpert DualStream 19 at $56,095, let you keep the swim end cooler and the hot tub end at soaking temperature, which is more efficient than heating one large body of water for both jobs.

Almost every swim spa we deliver in this region goes in by crane, and in the subdivisions of south Barrie, Innisfil and Bradford that usually means a lift over the house from the street on delivery day. On larger rural and lakefront lots we can sometimes back the truck to the pad. Either way you need a reinforced concrete pad or an engineered deck, and the town or township will want to see a permit and pool fencing, so check the requirements where you live early. We book the crane and coordinate with your electrician and contractor.

faq.q: Can I install a swim spa at a lakefront cottage?
faq.a: Yes, and it is a popular choice on Lake Simcoe where the water is cold and weedy for much of the season. The main constraints are hydro capacity, since a swim spa needs a dedicated 50 or 60 amp circuit, and crane access on a treed waterfront lot. Shoreline setbacks are enforced by the township and sometimes the conservation authority, so confirm placement before you pour a pad.

faq.q: Should I sink the swim spa into the ground or build a deck around it?
faq.a: Partial in-ground installs look best and make getting in easy, but the frost line here is deep and the excavation needs proper drainage and a vault you can still access for service. A raised deck built to the rim of the spa is the more common choice in Barrie backyards and avoids the groundwater problems that come with our spring thaw. We can share drawings your contractor can work from.

faq.q: Do I need to winterize a swim spa?
faq.a: No. A swim spa is built to run all year and it is easier on the equipment to keep it heated than to drain it. If you are away for weeks at a time, lower the set point and leave it running; the connected Jacuzzi models will alert you if anything changes. Draining is only for a cottage that loses hydro over winter, and we can walk you through that.

faq.q: How does a swim spa handle heavy snow?
faq.a: The hard cover carries a normal load, but a swim spa cover is large, so sweep it after a big squall rather than letting a week of snow sit on it. Place the spa where roof runoff and drifting will not bury one side. Owners who use theirs daily in winter tell us the routine is a two minute broom and a quick walk on a cleared path.

faq.q: Which swim spa is best for a family with young kids?
faq.a: The 13 foot Jacuzzi J-13 PowerPlay at $33,195 with eight seats, or the 12 foot J-12 Flow at $30,695, gives you a shallow, warm play area with a gentler current than the PowerPro lane. Both fit a standard subdivision backyard. Older kids on swim teams outgrow them and want the stronger current of a 14 or 16 foot PowerActive or PowerPro.

sauna.intro: Six months of real winter make this good sauna country. Clearlight infrared cabins go in a basement or garage and plug in; Serenity cedar saunas sit outside beside the snowbank the way they do in Finland.
body: The outdoor sauna has deep roots in this part of Ontario, and a Serenity cedar sauna on a rural lot in Oro-Medonte or a Georgian Bay waterfront in Midland fits the landscape. The Serenity Sauna at $17,495 seats a family; the Serenity Mini at $14,995 suits a couple or a smaller cottage lot. Heaters are sold separately, and the choice matters here: a wood burning heater needs no hydro at all, which is exactly what an off grid or hydro limited cottage wants, while an electric heater on a dedicated 240V circuit is the easy option for a Barrie backyard.

Indoors, Clearlight infrared is what commuters and shift workers around here buy for recovery after long drives and long days. A Sanctuary 2 at $11,795 fits a basement corner in a south Barrie or Innisfil two storey and runs off a standard outlet, and paired with a Chill Tubs Essential it gives you the hot and cold contrast in one corner of the house. Townhome and condo owners in the downtown and waterfront buildings choose the Sanctuary 1 at $10,495 because it fits through a standard door and assembles in an afternoon.

Outdoor saunas need a level base above grade so spring melt does not sit against the cedar, and in the snow belt a small roof overhang or a covered walkway from the house is worth planning. Site the door away from the prevailing wind and leave room for a cold plunge or a snowbank beside it, because that is half the point. The cabin is delivered in panels and assembled on site by our crew, usually in a day. Check with your township on accessory structure setbacks before you pick the spot; the rules differ between Barrie, Innisfil and the rural townships.

faq.q: Can I heat an outdoor sauna with wood at a cottage?
faq.a: Yes, and many cottage owners on Lake Simcoe and Georgian Bay do exactly that because it costs nothing in hydro and works during a power outage. A wood burning heater needs a proper chimney and clearances, and your insurer may want to know about it, so tell them. Firewood is easy to find around here and a sauna burns far less than a woodstove.

faq.q: How do I keep an outdoor sauna dry through the spring thaw?
faq.a: Set it on a gravel bed with patio stones or a small deck so meltwater drains away from the base, and leave a gap between the cabin and any fence for airflow. Cedar handles moisture well but standing water at the sill will shorten its life. Open the door and vent after each session, especially in the damp weeks of March and April.

faq.q: Will an infrared sauna heat up in an unheated garage in January?
faq.a: It will, but slowly, and the cabin loses heat to a cold room. Most owners in this climate put the Clearlight in a basement or a finished room where the ambient temperature stays above about 15 degrees. If the garage is your only option, insulate the space or plan on a longer warm-up through the winter.

faq.q: Which sauna works in a townhome or condo?
faq.a: The Clearlight Sanctuary 1 or Sanctuary 2 is the usual pick in the townhomes off Mapleview and the condos downtown and along the waterfront. Both plug into a standard outlet, need no venting and sit on any flat floor. Check with your condo board about assembly and weight limits before you order, and measure the doorway and any turns in the hallway.

faq.q: How long does it take to get a Serenity sauna delivered and built?
faq.a: Lead times vary with cedar grade and heater choice, so ask for the current timeline when you order. Late spring through fall is the busy season for outdoor builds; winter builds are possible on a cleared, level base. Our crew assembles the panelled cabin on site, and your electrician connects the heater afterward if you chose electric.

hot-tub.small: A small tub is the cottage tub here. The Nordic Sport All-In-110V at $7,295 and Retreat All-In-110V at $9,195 run off a dedicated standard outlet, so a lake place with an older 100 amp panel and electric baseboards can still have a hot tub without a service upgrade. The Jacuzzi J-315 at $18,795 and J-404L at $25,195 are the pick for a couple in a downtown townhome or a retirement bungalow in Alcona where two people soak most nights and the yard is small. Both fit through a standard gate on a dolly.
hot-tub.medium: Five and six seat tubs are the everyday Simcoe County backyard tub. The Jacuzzi J-335 at $21,995 is the one we sell most to commuter families in the new builds along Mapleview and in Innisfil; the J-235 at $16,295 does the same job for less. The Aquasolus The Eden at $13,995 comes with White Glove delivery and setup included, which matters on a rural lot. If you want the SmartTub app to warm the tub from the car on the 400, look at the J-435 floor model at $24,995 or the J-408L at $29,995.
hot-tub.large: Seven seats and up is what the cottage crowd and the big blended families buy. The Jacuzzi J-509 at $39,595 with 76 jets is the flagship for a large new build or a lakefront place where the whole family gathers on a long weekend. The J-495 floor model at $31,395 gives you nine seats for far less, and the J-385 at $26,595 or J-245 at $16,295 are the sensible family picks. On Georgian Bay and Lake Simcoe properties a big tub almost always goes in by crane, so we survey the lot first and price the lift into the quote.

productNotes.swim-spa: Swim spas in this region are bought by two groups: swimmers and triathletes who lose Lake Simcoe from October to June, and families who want a pool without a pool contractor and a five month season. The Jacuzzi J-19 PowerPro at $58,995 and the SwimLife SwimExpert AquaStream 17 at $50,095 are the training choices; the J-13 PowerPlay at $33,195 and J-12 Flow at $30,695 are the family choices. All of them run through the winter, and on a deck against the house they double as a very large hot tub after skiing.
productNotes.sauna: Sauna buyers around here split cleanly. Cottage owners and rural households in Oro-Medonte, Midland and Collingwood want a Serenity cedar sauna outdoors, usually with a wood burning heater at the lake and an electric one in town. Commuters, hospital and college staff and the fitness crowd want a Clearlight Sanctuary infrared cabin in the basement for daily recovery. The Sanctuary 2 at $11,795 and Sanctuary Y at $13,995 pair well with a Chill Tubs Essential, which is the fastest way into a hot and cold routine without building anything outside.
productNotes.cold-plunge: Cold plunge came naturally to a region where people already jump in the lake in May. The Chill Tubs Essential Bath and Essential Pod are the entry points, the Obsidian and the Pro are the chilled, filtered units for daily use, and all four are priced in the showroom rather than online. They pair with a Serenity outdoor sauna on a rural lot or a Clearlight cabin in the basement, and they run all year on a standard outlet. Come try one on the floor; it is a different conversation once you have been in.

financing: Most of our Barrie customers finance, and the pattern is practical: a bi-weekly payment that fits alongside a mortgage on a new build in Innisfil or Bradford, or a second payment for a cottage tub that goes up the 400 in May. The Nordic Retreat All-In-110V works out from $18.62 bi-weekly and the Sport from $15.01, which for many cottage owners is less than the propane they burn on a long weekend. Approval is quick, terms are shown on every product page, and you can apply in the showroom on Bryne Drive or from home before you drive up.
showroom: The showroom is on Bryne Drive in south Barrie, just off Highway 400 at Mapleview, which puts it on the way to nearly everywhere in Simcoe County. Cottage traffic passes it on Friday afternoon and Innisfil and Bradford commuters pass it every day. Every hot tub, swim spa and sauna on the floor is heated and running, so you can sit in a J-385, feel the current in a swim spa and step into a Serenity cedar cabin on the same visit.

Bring your lot measurements, a photo of the gate and side yard, and a picture of your electrical panel if you can; with those our team can tell you on the spot whether it is a dolly or a crane job and roughly what the electrical run will cost. Cottage owners should bring the road name and whether it is plowed in winter. Wet tests are welcome by appointment, and if you are coming from Orillia, Collingwood or Midland we will make sure the models you want to compare are running when you arrive.

Innisfil.lead: Innisfil is our closest service area and one of our busiest, from the new subdivisions in Alcona to the Lake Simcoe shoreline between Big Bay Point and Gilford.
body: Housing here splits between fast growing subdivision streets in Alcona and Lefroy with tight lots and rear yards backing onto other rear yards, and older lake lots on the shore roads with mature trees and long, narrow driveways. Subdivision deliveries are usually a straightforward dolly job through a rear gate, and the panel is close. The shore properties are more often a crane lift, and if the hydro is an older service we look at a Nordic 110V or plan a service upgrade with the electrician.

Innisfil buyers are commuters who drive the 400 to Vaughan and Toronto and want the tub hot when they get home, and Lake Simcoe cottage owners who have turned a summer place into a year round home. The Jacuzzi J-335 and J-385 are the most common picks in the subdivisions. On the shoreline, where the yard is bigger and the family shows up all summer, the seven seat J-485 and the eight seat J-509 make sense. Well water is common outside the serviced areas, so ask us about fill filters.
Innisfil.drive: Take Yonge Street or Highway 400 north to Mapleview Drive, then head west to Bryne Drive; from Alcona it is about twenty minutes.

Orillia.lead: Orillia sits between Lake Couchiching and Lake Simcoe at the top of Highway 11, a forty minute run down to our Barrie showroom and a market with its own strong cottage culture.
body: The city itself has a lot of older homes near the downtown and the waterfront with deep, narrow lots and detached garages, plus newer subdivisions on the west side toward Highway 11. Older lots often mean a walk down a side yard with a dolly, or a small crane over a garage. The surrounding cottage roads on Couchiching, the Severn and the north end of Simcoe are where the bigger crane jobs are, and where seasonal road access shapes when we can deliver.

Orillia buyers include retirees who moved up from the GTA and want a comfortable six seater like the J-355 or J-435 for two people most nights, university and hospital staff who want a Clearlight infrared for recovery, and cottage families who want the biggest tub the hydro will carry. Water care differs street by street: municipal supply in town, wells and lake draw at many cottages. We stock the treatment products for both and set the tub up accordingly.
Orillia.drive: Highway 11 south becomes Highway 400 at Barrie; stay on the 400 south to the Mapleview exit and turn west to Bryne Drive, about forty minutes from downtown Orillia.

Alliston.lead: Alliston and the rest of New Tecumseth are a mix of long established town streets, farm properties and newer subdivisions filled with people who work at the Honda plant or commute south.
body: Lots in the older part of town are generous by subdivision standards, with room for a tub off a back deck and a side yard wide enough for a dolly. The newer subdivisions on the edges are tighter and the delivery is planned around the gate width and the air conditioner placement. Farm and rural properties between Alliston, Beeton and Tottenham have all the space in the world but often a long run to the panel and a well, so we plan the electrical and the water care before delivery day.

Shift workers are a big part of the Alliston market, and a tub they can use at odd hours without waking the house is the ask: a six seater like the Jacuzzi J-335 or the Aquasolus The Eden with White Glove setup included. Rural families lean to the seven seat J-385 or the Wellness Shop Ontario S104, and a Serenity outdoor cedar sauna is a natural fit on a farm lot with room and firewood to spare.
Alliston.drive: Follow Highway 89 east to Highway 400 at Cookstown, head north to the Mapleview exit and turn west; the drive from Alliston is around forty minutes in normal traffic.

Midland.lead: Midland and Penetanguishene sit on Severn Sound at the edge of Georgian Bay, in the heart of the snow belt and surrounded by some of the most popular cottage country in Ontario.
body: Waterfront and cottage properties dominate the calls we get from here: sloped lots down to the Bay, treed lanes, seasonal roads in Tiny and Tay, and hydro that was sized for a summer cabin. Crane delivery is the norm rather than the exception, and we time deliveries around spring load restrictions and fall road closures. In town, older homes on the streets above the harbour have decent yards and municipal water, which keeps the job simple.

The snow off Georgian Bay is heavier here than in Barrie, so we talk about cover lifters, roof runoff and placement before we talk about jets. Cottage owners choose the Nordic Retreat All-In-110V for a weekend place with light hydro, or a Jacuzzi J-245 or J-285 where the panel can take a 240V circuit and the whole family comes up. This is also our strongest market for a Serenity outdoor sauna with a wood burning heater, which fits the setting and works when the power goes out.
Midland.drive: Take Highway 93 south to Highway 400, continue south and exit at Mapleview, then turn west to Bryne Drive; plan on about fifty minutes from Midland harbour.

Collingwood.lead: Collingwood combines a lively downtown, the ski hills at Blue Mountain and a Georgian Bay waterfront, and hot tubs here are as much ski equipment as backyard furniture.
body: The market is unusual: chalets and townhomes near the hill that are used on winter weekends, established homes in town with mature lots, and waterfront condos and new builds along the Bay. Chalet deliveries are often crane lifts on sloped, treed lots with a driveway full of cars, and the tub has to be placed where a January dump does not bury the steps. Townhome and condo owners tend to look at a Clearlight infrared cabin or a compact tub like the J-315 that fits a small patio.

Skiers want heat fast and a tub big enough for a house full of guests, which is why the Jacuzzi J-485 and J-495 do well here, and the SmartTub app that brings the tub up to temperature before you leave the hill gets used constantly. Year round residents are often retirees and remote workers who use the tub daily and appreciate the lower running cost of a well insulated Jacuzzi. Check with the town on setbacks; Collingwood and the Blue Mountains have their own rules for accessory structures.
Collingwood.drive: Highway 26 east through Stayner brings you into north Barrie; join Highway 400 south to the Mapleview exit and turn west, roughly an hour door to door.

Wasaga Beach.lead: Wasaga Beach is a beach town that has become a year round community, with new subdivisions inland and older cottages along the Nottawasaga River and the shore of Georgian Bay.
body: Housing is a mix of small original cottages on sandy lots, retirement bungalows in the newer subdivisions off Mosley Street and River Road, and a growing number of families who moved up for the price of a house. Sandy soil makes for easy digging but calls for a properly compacted base under any pad; a tub that settles unevenly will not drain right. Many lots are flat with good access, so a dolly delivery through a side gate is more common here than in Collingwood.

The people buying here are retirees who want a five or six seater like the Jacuzzi J-325 or J-335 for daily soaks and grandchildren on weekends, and young families who came for affordability and want a full size tub without a full size price, which is where the Aquasolus The Cove at $11,995 and the Wellness Shop Ontario S104 at $15,595 come in. Lake effect snow is heavy here, so a cover lifter and a sheltered placement are part of every quote.
Wasaga Beach.drive: Take Highway 26 east or County Road 92 through Elmvale to reach Highway 400 in north Barrie, then south to Mapleview and west to Bryne Drive; about forty five minutes from the beach.

Bradford.lead: Bradford is the southern edge of our territory, a fast growing commuter town beside the Holland Marsh with its own GO station and a Highway 400 interchange at Highway 88.
body: Almost everything built in Bradford in the last fifteen years is a subdivision home on a compact lot, with a rear yard that backs onto a neighbour and a gate that is usually wide enough for a dolly but not always. We measure gates and check for air conditioner units and window wells before delivery. The older streets near downtown and the farm properties out toward the Marsh give you more room and, in the rural cases, a well and a longer electrical run.

Bradford buyers are almost all commuters, many driving to Vaughan, Newmarket or downtown Toronto every day, and the ask is a tub the family can use on weeknights without a lot of fuss: the Jacuzzi J-335 at $21,995 and J-235 at $16,295 are the two we sell most here. Households with teenagers step up to a J-385. Our Vaughan showroom is also within reach, but Barrie is the stop if you want to see the full swim spa and sauna floor on your way north.
Bradford.drive: Highway 400 north from the Highway 88 interchange to the Mapleview exit, then west to Bryne Drive; about twenty five minutes outside rush hour.

Angus.lead: Angus is a Township of Essa community on the Nottawasaga River west of Barrie, next to Base Borden, with newer subdivisions and a long history as a military family town.
body: Lots here are a mix of newer subdivision homes with modest rear yards and older properties on larger lots near the river, plus rural acreages on the concession roads toward Baxter and Thornton. Subdivision deliveries are routine dolly jobs. On the acreages the tub is often a long way from the house panel, so we get the electrician involved early, and most of those properties are on wells that run hard, which changes the start-up water care.

Military families post in and out, and they tell us they want a tub that is easy to own and easy to sell or move: the Jacuzzi J-235 and the Aquasolus The Calma are popular for that reason. Longer term residents on rural lots take the seven seat J-345 or J-365 and often add a Serenity outdoor cedar sauna where they have the space. Angus is close enough to Barrie that scheduling is simple once the pad and electrical are ready.
Angus.drive: Head east on Highway 90 into Barrie, then take Essa Road south to Bryne Drive, or hop on the 400 south one exit to Mapleview; around twenty minutes.

Oro-Medonte.lead: Oro-Medonte is the township between Barrie and Orillia, stretching from the Lake Simcoe shore at Shanty Bay and Hawkestone up to the ski hills at Horseshoe Valley and Mount St. Louis Moonstone.
body: Almost every property here is rural or waterfront: estate lots on the concession roads, lakefront homes and cottages on the shore roads, and chalets and new builds around Horseshoe Valley. Space is rarely the problem. Distance to the panel, well water and winter access are. Long driveways mean we can often bring the truck right to the pad, but sloped shore lots still need a crane. Nearly all of the township is on wells, so pre-filtering the fill water and a start-up metal treatment are standard on our deliveries here.

The ski hill neighbourhoods buy tubs for after the last run and want them big and hot: the Jacuzzi J-485 and J-495 are the fit, and the SmartTub app matters when the house sits empty midweek. Lakeshore residents, many of them retirees, prefer a six seater like the J-375 or J-445 for daily use. On the estate lots a Serenity outdoor sauna with a wood or electric heater is a common addition beside the tub, and there is room for a proper cold plunge next to both.
Oro-Medonte.drive: From Horseshoe Valley Road or the lakeshore, join Highway 11 south into Barrie, continue on Highway 400 south to Mapleview and turn west; twenty to thirty five minutes depending on where you start.

Newmarket.lead: Newmarket is a York Region town of established neighbourhoods and newer subdivisions, home to a regional hospital and a busy GO line, and the southernmost community we serve from Barrie.
body: Housing is mostly mature suburban streets with decent size lots and fenced yards, plus newer, tighter subdivisions on the edges and a growing number of townhomes near Davis Drive and Yonge Street. Older lots often have a side yard wide enough for a dolly; townhomes and the newer streets are more often a crane over the garage. Municipal water keeps water care simple, and the panel is rarely far from the back wall.

Hospital staff, commuters on the 404 and the GO, and families with kids in sports are the core buyers, and they want a tub for recovery and weeknight use: the Jacuzzi J-335 and J-355 are the usual picks, and a Clearlight Sanctuary 2 in the basement is the sauna choice. Newmarket sits between our Barrie and Vaughan showrooms; come to Bryne Drive if you are heading north anyway or want to talk through a cottage install, because a lot of Newmarket families also own a place up north.
Newmarket.drive: Take Davis Drive west to Highway 400, head north to the Mapleview exit and turn west to Bryne Drive; about thirty five minutes without traffic.

productBlurbs.j-509: Eight seats and 76 jets make this the tub for a Lake Simcoe waterfront place where three generations show up on the long weekend. The open layout means nobody argues over a lounger, and True Water with ProClarity six stage filtration keeps up when the tub is full every night of July. Most shoreline lots need a crane, so we survey the property first and build the lift into the quote. Sale price is $39,595.
productBlurbs.j-508: A Horseshoe Valley chalet fills up on ski weekends, and seven open seats with 56 jets means everyone off the hill gets a spot at once. The SmartTub app lets you bring it up to temperature from the parking lot before the last run. Compared with the J-509 you give up one seat and 20 jets and keep the same ProClarity six stage water care, at $35,695 rather than the flagship's price.
productBlurbs.j-508l: Six seats at 60 jets is the most jet coverage per seat in the J-500 line, which suits an Oro-Medonte estate lot where a couple soaks every night and the extended family visits on holidays. Long driveways on the concession roads often let our truck reach the pad directly, saving a crane. Well water is nearly universal in the township, so we set up a fill pre-filter alongside the True Water system at delivery.
productBlurbs.j-408: Families in the Alcona subdivisions of Innisfil ask for a seven seater the kids can pile into after hockey, and the J-408 delivers that with 41 jets in an open layout that fits a compact rear yard. The J4 cabinet clears a six foot gate on a dolly, and the panel in a new build is usually on the back wall, so the electrical run stays short. Priced at $29,995 on sale.
productBlurbs.j-408l: Commuters who spend an hour on Highway 400 each way want the tub hot the moment they walk in, and the SmartTub app on this six seat lounger does exactly that from the car. Two people get the lounge and the corner seats most weeknights, while 39 jets and the ProClarity five stage filter handle a full house on Saturday. The open seating J-408 costs the same, so the choice is purely lounger or no lounger.
productBlurbs.j-404l: Couples in the condos and townhomes along Kempenfelt Bay downtown tend to want a lounger and not much else, and this four seat J4 gives them 32 jets in a footprint that fits a small patio. It clears the standard six foot gate on a dolly and needs a short 240V run. At $25,195 it is the least expensive way into the J4 series with True Water care.
productBlurbs.j-495: Nine seats is chalet territory. Blue Mountain weekend houses in Collingwood host a crowd, and the 71 jet J-495 seats all of them without anyone perching on the edge. The 2025 floor model is clearing at $31,395, which is real money off the current stock price for the same open layout and ProClarity five stage filtration. Deliveries on the treed, sloped lots near the hill are crane jobs, and we schedule them around the ski season traffic.
productBlurbs.j-485: Georgian Bay cottage families in Tiny Township who come up every weekend from May to Thanksgiving want seven open seats with enough jets to matter, and 49 jets across this J-400 model do the job. The 2025 floor model at $26,295 makes it a serious alternative to a J-300 for a place where the whole family soaks. Seasonal road access decides the delivery date, so we book around the spring half load season.
productBlurbs.j-475: Nurses and paramedics coming off a night shift at Southlake in Newmarket told us the lounge seat is the one that gets used, and the J-475 puts a full body lounger in a seven seat layout with 55 jets. It shares a price with the open seating J-485 at $30,795, and both are True Water tubs with ProClarity five stage filtration. Mature Newmarket lots usually give us a side yard wide enough for a dolly.
productBlurbs.j-445: Retirees in the newer bungalows off Mosley Street in Wasaga Beach soak daily as a couple and have grandchildren on weekends, which is the exact pattern six open seats and 45 jets are built for. Nobody is stuck in a lounger they do not fit, and the ProClarity five stage filtration handles the sunscreen after a beach day. The 2025 floor model is clearing at $23,995, and flat, sandy Wasaga lots usually allow a dolly delivery.
productBlurbs.j-435: Bradford commuters heading to Vaughan and back every day want a six seater with a lounger and an app, and the J-435 gives you 47 jets, a lounge seat and SmartTub so the water is ready when the GO train pulls in. The 2025 floor model at $24,995 is the way to get J-400 build quality on a subdivision budget. We measure the rear gate and check for air conditioner clearance before delivery day.
productBlurbs.j-385: The Mapleview and Big Bay Point subdivisions are full of families who want a seven seater that fits a standard rear yard, and the J-385 is the one we sell most to them. Fifty one jets in an open layout, CLEARRAY Active Oxygen water care and a ProClear skimming weir keep the tub clean with kids in it every evening. Sale price is $26,595, and it clears a six foot gate on a dolly.
productBlurbs.j-365: Rural lots around Angus and the Essa concession roads have room for a seven seater and a well that runs hard, so on this 46 jet J-300 we install a fill pre-filter and a metal treatment at start-up. The open layout suits long term residents who host neighbours more than they soak alone. Versus the J-385 you give up five jets and pay less, with the sale price at $24,795.
productBlurbs.j-345: Shift workers at the Honda plant in Alliston get home at odd hours and want a tub they can slip into without waking the house, and the entry point to seven open seats in the J-300 series is this 41 jet model. CLEARRAY Active Oxygen means less chemical smell drifting toward the bedroom window at two in the morning. It is the least expensive seven seater in the J-300 range at $23,195.
productBlurbs.j-375: Lakeshore retirees in Orillia who moved up from the GTA usually soak as a pair and want the lounger to be the best seat in the tub, and 52 jets across six seats make this the most jetted J-300 lounger. Deep, narrow lots near the Orillia waterfront often mean a dolly walk down the side yard or a small crane over a detached garage, which we sort out on the site visit. Sale price $25,295.
productBlurbs.j-355: Commuters riding the GO from Newmarket get home late, and a six seat lounger they can fall into at nine o'clock is what they ask for. This J-300 gives them 44 jets and a lounge seat at $24,795, the same price as the seven seat open J-365 if you would rather trade the lounger for an extra spot. Municipal water in Newmarket keeps the CLEARRAY Active Oxygen routine simple.
productBlurbs.j-335: Young families in the new builds around Painswick and Holly buy this six seat lounger more than any other tub on our floor, because it fits the rear yard of a forty foot lot and still has 42 jets and a lounge seat. It runs on a standard 240V circuit with a short run to the basement panel, and the J-300 CLEARRAY Active Oxygen system suits a busy household. On sale at $21,995.
productBlurbs.j-325: A five seat open tub with 23 jets is what a grandparent in Wasaga Beach wants: room for two every evening, room for the grandkids on a Sunday, and no lounger taking up a spot nobody uses. The shell is compact enough to drop onto an existing deck off a bungalow, and at $20,495 it is the lowest priced route into the J-300 series with its ProClear filtration.
productBlurbs.j-315: Townhomes near the Blue Mountain base in Collingwood have small patios and owners who ski hard, and this three seat lounger with 23 jets is built for exactly that: one person stretched out, two more in the corner seats, and the whole thing tucked against the wall. The compact footprint keeps snow clearing to a minimum after a January dump. It is the smallest J-300 and sells at $18,795.
productBlurbs.j-285: Midland cottage families whose panel can carry a 240V circuit step up from the plug and play tubs to this seven seat open J-200 with 42 jets, the most in the series. CLEARRAY UV-C water care needs less attention when the place sits empty midweek. On sale at $18,695, it costs less than any seven seater in the J-300 line while keeping the Jacuzzi warranty. Crane delivery over a cottage roof is routine for our crews on Severn Sound.
productBlurbs.j-245: Farm families out toward the Holland Marsh near Bradford tell us they want seven seats, a proper Jacuzzi warranty and not a lot else, which describes this open 37 jet J-200 at $16,295. Long runs to the panel on a farm property are planned with the electrician before delivery, and well water gets a fill pre-filter. The J-285 adds five jets for more money if you host a lot.
productBlurbs.j-275: Skiers coming down from Snow Valley on a Sunday afternoon want a lounger and quick heat, and the 2025 clearance stock on this six seat J-200 starts at $14,695, which puts a 38 jet Jacuzzi lounger at a price normally reserved for the five seat models. CLEARRAY UV-C water care handles the sweat and sunscreen of a house full of weekend guests. Floor clearance units go fast; ask which ones are still on the Bryne Drive floor.
productBlurbs.j-235: Lefroy and the south end of Innisfil are commuter country, and this six seat lounger with 34 jets is the everyday tub we deliver to those subdivision streets. It shares a $16,295 sale price with the seven seat open J-245, so the decision is whether one person wants to lie flat or the family wants an extra seat. A rear gate check and a photo of your panel is all we need to quote delivery.
productBlurbs.j-225: Older homes in Allandale have mature trees and a narrow side yard, and this five seat open J-200 with 26 jets fits down that walk on a dolly where a bigger shell would need a crane. Georgian College staff and couples who soak most nights find five open seats plenty. CLEARRAY UV-C water care and ProClassic filtration keep the routine simple on Barrie municipal water. Priced at $14,695.
productBlurbs.j-215: Orillia's older streets above the waterfront have deep lots and small patios, and a couple there needs a lounger, not a party tub. This three seat J-200 puts 21 jets on one lounge and two corner seats and sits at $14,095, the lowest priced Jacuzzi lounger we sell. It clears any side gate on a dolly and works well on a small raised deck off the kitchen.
productBlurbs.retreat-all-in-110v: Cottages on Lake Couchiching with a 100 amp panel and electric baseboards cannot spare a 50 amp circuit, and the Retreat All-In-110V solves that with a 15 amp plug and play cord that goes into a dedicated standard outlet. Five open seats and 13 jets are plenty for a weekend place, and the Nordic Clean ozonator keeps water manageable between visits. It runs from $18.62 bi-weekly OAC, and the round shell rides easily on a trailer up Highway 11.
productBlurbs.sport-all-in-110v: Seasonal road cottages around Penetanguishene get used from May to October, and a $7,295 plug and play round tub that heats slowly and runs off the outlet already on the deck is the sensible buy. Five seats, 15 jets and a GFCI cord included means no electrician visit and no service upgrade. Compared with the Retreat All-In-110V you get two more jets and pay less, with the same Nordic Clean Ozone water care.
productBlurbs.retreat-se: Military families posting through Base Borden want a tub that installs fast, sells easily and does not need a crane, and the Retreat SE on a 220V 40 amp circuit is that tub. Five open seats and 29 jets, more than double what the plug and play Retreat All-In-110V carries, give it a real massage. Nordic Pure Ozone keeps water care simple in Angus, where wells run hard. It works out from $19.38 bi-weekly OAC.
productBlurbs.ontario-s106: Well water households in Oro-Medonte want a big tub that shrugs off winter, and the Ontario S106 brings seven open seats, 59 jets and two 6 HP pumps built in the USA, wrapped in Thermal Shield insulation for the nights when Highway 11 is closed with snow. The 50 square foot flow through filter handles the sediment a rural well leaves behind. Sale price is $17,695.
productBlurbs.ontario-s104: Young families who moved to Wasaga Beach for the price of a house want a full size seven seater without a Jacuzzi budget, and the S104 at $15,595 is the answer: 54 jets, two 6 HP pumps and Thermal Shield insulation against lake effect snow. It trails the S106 by five jets and costs less. On a flat sandy Wasaga lot, delivery is usually a dolly through the side gate.
productBlurbs.ontario-l-s103: Acreage owners around Thornton and Stroud with a long electrical run tend to pick the L S103 for its lounger, since one person on a rural lot soaks alone most nights and six seats cover the rest. Fifty one jets on two 6 HP pumps deliver more massage than most tubs at $15,595, and Thermal Shield insulation matters on an exposed concession road where the wind has nothing to stop it.
productBlurbs.ontario-l-s105: Nurses at Royal Victoria in Barrie finish twelve hour shifts and want a lounger with real pressure behind it, and the L S105 backs its 56 jets with two 6 HP pumps and a GECKO K1000 keypad that is simple to read at eleven at night. Against the L S103 you gain five jets and the better keypad for $17,695. Thermal Shield insulation keeps the February hydro bill in check.
productBlurbs.the-brook: Townhome owners in Ardagh Bluffs have a patio the size of a parking spot, and The Brook is the four seat Aquasolus that fits it while still delivering 23 jets and an ozone system. White Glove delivery and setup is included, worth up to $1,900, which on a tight townhome lot with a shared fence line is not a small thing. It is the lowest priced European built tub on our floor at $10,995.
productBlurbs.the-cove: Bradford new builds have rear yards that back onto the neighbour and a family that wants seven seats without the payment that usually comes with them. The Cove gives you a full size open layout with 27 jets from Superior Wellness in Europe, with White Glove delivery and setup included, and it sells at $11,995. If the budget stretches, The Calma adds ten jets in the same seven seat format.
productBlurbs.the-calma: Families commuting from Tottenham and Beeton along Highway 9 want a seven seater for weeknights that does not need a crane or a second mortgage, and The Calma delivers 37 jets in an open layout that fits a subdivision yard. Superior Wellness builds it in Europe, our crew handles the White Glove setup, and the sale price is $13,995. Ozone water care keeps the chemical shelf short.
productBlurbs.the-eden: Alliston shift workers want a lounger they can slide into at seven in the morning after nights, and The Eden is the only Aquasolus with one. Six seats, 42 jets and ozone water care at $13,995, the same price as the open seating Calma, so the only question is whether the lounger earns its spot. White Glove delivery and setup is included on the rural lots between Alliston and Cookstown, where that saves real effort.
productBlurbs.j-19dt-powerpro: Triathletes on the Innisfil shoreline lose Lake Simcoe from October to June, and the 19 foot J-19DT PowerPro is the model they buy to keep training: a full PowerPro current at one end and a separate hot tub zone at the other, each on its own temperature. Fifty three jets, six seats and quad 50 square foot filtration mean the family gets a soak while you swim. It sells at $60,895 and needs a 20 amp plus 40 amp electrical setup.
productBlurbs.j-19-powerpro: Masters swimmers who train in Kempenfelt Bay all summer want the full 19 foot length and the strongest current, and the J-19 PowerPro gives them that in a single temperature pool with 34 jets and four seats for the cool down. CLEARRAY Active Oxygen plus dual 50 square foot filters keep up with daily laps. At $58,995 it costs less than the dual temperature J-19DT PowerPro if you do not need the hot tub end.
productBlurbs.j-16-powerpro: Sixteen feet is the length that fits between the house and the back fence on a south Barrie subdivision lot, which is why this PowerPro model with 34 jets and four seats goes in more often than the 19 footer around Mapleview. Delivery is a crane over the house from the street, booked with the electrician for the 40 amp circuit. The sale price is $54,295 with CLEARRAY Active Oxygen and dual filtration included.
productBlurbs.j-14-powerpro: Mature Newmarket lots have room for a 14 foot spa on a reinforced pad without losing the whole yard, and this PowerPro packs 51 jets and five seats into that length, so it works as a serious hot tub as well as a training pool. Kids in competitive swimming get a real current; parents get a soak after. At $48,795 it is the least expensive PowerPro, and the crane goes over the garage.
productBlurbs.j-19dt-poweractive: Horseshoe Valley chalets come alive after the last run, and the dual temperature J-19DT PowerActive gives the skiers a hot tub zone at soaking temperature while the swim end stays cooler for the morning workout. Six seats, 51 jets and four 50 square foot filters at $53,295, at a lower price than the PowerPro version of the same layout, with a gentler current that suits most recreational swimmers.
productBlurbs.j-19-poweractive: Estate lots on the Oro-Medonte concession roads often let our truck back right up to the pad, which removes the crane from the budget on a 19 foot spa like this one. The PowerActive current is strong enough for daily laps without the PowerPro price, with 32 jets, four seats and CLEARRAY Active Oxygen with dual 50 square foot filters. Sale price $51,395, on a single 40 amp circuit.
productBlurbs.j-16-poweractive: Remote workers who moved to Collingwood full time want a pool they can use at noon in February between calls, and the 16 foot PowerActive fits a town lot near the Bay with a current that suits fitness swimming rather than racing. Four seats and 32 jets, CLEARRAY Active Oxygen, one 40 amp circuit, and a sale price of $46,495. Snow off Georgian Bay means we talk cover placement early.
productBlurbs.j-14-poweractive: The newer subdivisions on the west side of Orillia toward Highway 11 have standard rear yards, and 14 feet is the length that leaves room for a patio. Five seats and 49 jets make this PowerActive the most hot tub like of the swim spas at $41,395, with a current that suits resistance walking and steady laps. Compared with the 14 foot PowerPro you trade some current strength for a lower price.
productBlurbs.j-13-powerplay: Innisfil families with young kids want warm shallow water and a lot of seats more than a racing current, and the 13 foot J-13 PowerPlay has eight of them with 38 jets. A 32 amp circuit keeps the electrical simpler than the bigger spas, and the shell still fits an Alcona rear yard on a reinforced pad. It sells at $33,195 and doubles as the biggest hot tub in the neighbourhood.
productBlurbs.j-12-flow: Retirees in Wasaga Beach who use the spa for resistance walking and gentle laps rather than sprint sets do well with the 12 foot J-12 Flow, the shortest and lowest priced swim spa on our floor at $30,695. Eight seats and 31 jets make it a warm, social tub for the grandchildren, and CLEARRAY UV-C with a 50 square foot DFML filter keeps water care simple. It fits a sandy bungalow lot with room to spare.
productBlurbs.swimexpert-dualstream-19: A Georgian Bay cottage near Midland with a family of swimmers and a family of soakers wants both ends of the DualStream 19: a 19 foot swim lane with 53 jets and an attached five person hot tub with its own 30 jets and separate controls. ClearStream mineral water care means less chemical hauling up a seasonal road. On sale at $56,095, it needs a 20 amp and a 40 amp circuit and a crane on most waterfront lots.
productBlurbs.swimexpert-aquastream-17: Bradford commuters who leave on the early GO and get home in the dark want a lane they can swim in before the train, and the 17 foot AquaStream with 30 jets and three seats fits a subdivision lot better than a 19 footer while keeping a real training current. ClearStream mineral care keeps the water gentle on skin through a cold winter. Sale price is $50,095 on a single 40 amp circuit.
productBlurbs.swimexpert-swimstream-14: Rural Essa properties around Angus sometimes have a panel that cannot spare 40 amps, and the 14 foot SwimStream runs on a 32 amp circuit while still giving a swimmer 30 jets of current and three seats to cool down. It is the shortest SwimExpert and the lowest priced at $44,795, with ClearStream mineral water care that plays well with hard well water. Long driveways on the concession roads often let the truck reach the pad.
productBlurbs.swimfit-aquastream-17: Honda plant employees in Alliston who swim before a day shift want a 17 foot lane at a price closer to a hot tub, and the SwimFit AquaStream at $43,795 gives them 28 jets and three seats on a 40 amp circuit. Against the SwimExpert AquaStream 17 you give up two jets and save on the sticker, with the same ClearStream mineral system. Older Alliston lots are generous, so crane costs stay reasonable.
productBlurbs.swimfit-swimstream-14: Barrie east end homeowners doing physio walking against a gentle current use a 14 foot SwimFit for exactly that, and it fits the mature lots off Grove Street where a longer spa would not. Twenty eight jets, three seats and ClearStream mineral water care on a 32 amp circuit, at $38,095, the lowest priced swim spa from SwimLife on our floor. Street to pad is a short crane on most east end lots.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-1: Condos along the Barrie waterfront have a spare corner and a standard door, and the Sanctuary 1 is the Clearlight cabin that fits both: a one person full spectrum infrared sauna that runs on a household circuit and assembles in an afternoon. It comes with a free AROMA ONE aromatherapy diffuser and sells at $10,495, with the lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters. Check with the condo board on weight and assembly before you order.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-2: Highway 400 commuters who get home stiff from ninety minutes in the car buy the Sanctuary 2 for the basement more than any other Clearlight cabin. Two people fit the full spectrum infrared bench, it plugs into a standard outlet, and there is no venting to run through a finished ceiling. The sale price is $11,795, and it pairs with a Chill Tubs Essential for a full contrast routine in one corner of the house.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-3: Snowmobilers who ride the Simcoe County trails all weekend come home cold to the bone, and a three person Sanctuary 3 in the garage entry or mudroom warms them back up on full spectrum infrared. It is the smallest Clearlight cabin that seats a whole family of riders, in Basswood or Mahogany, and sells at $12,995 with True Wave heaters carrying a lifetime warranty.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-5: Southlake hospital staff in Newmarket who want an infrared cabin the whole family can use choose the Sanctuary 5, the five seat step up in the Clearlight range at $13,995. Full spectrum infrared heat with True Wave heaters, Basswood or Mahogany, and a lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters. It fits a finished room in the mature streets off Yonge and takes the edge off a twelve hour shift for more than one person at a time.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-y: Hockey families spend October to March in cold rinks across Simcoe County, and a four person Sanctuary Y in the basement is where the whole household thaws out afterward. Full spectrum infrared warms bodies rather than air, so it is ready quickly on a school night. It seats four, comes in Basswood or Mahogany, and the sale price is $13,995, the same as the three person Sanctuary 5.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-c: Collingwood ski chalets have a finished lower level and four people coming off Blue Mountain at once, and the four person Sanctuary C at $14,495 fits the corner of that rec room. Full spectrum infrared heats you through quickly after a cold day on the hill, in Basswood or Mahogany with True Wave heaters and a lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters. Assembly happens in an afternoon, so it is ready for the next weekend.
productBlurbs.sanctuary-retreat: Estate homes in Oro-Medonte often have a dedicated wellness room, and the Sanctuary Retreat is the Clearlight flagship for it: four people on full spectrum infrared in Basswood or Mahogany, at $15,295, the top of the Sanctuary range. Families who ski Mount St. Louis Moonstone midweek use it every evening through the winter, and the lifetime warranty on cabin and True Wave heaters means it outlasts the rest of the room.
productBlurbs.serenity-mini: Lake Couchiching cottages with room beside the dock and a hydro service that cannot take another load are where the Serenity Mini with a wood burning heater shines. Canadian made from cedar, it seats a couple on an open bench and runs up to 194 degrees. Knotty cedar pricing is $14,995 with the heater sold separately; clear cedar is available. Our crew assembles the panels on a gravel base above the spring melt line.
productBlurbs.serenity-sauna: Waterfront properties in Tiny and Tay near Midland are where the full size Serenity Sauna lives best, an outdoor cedar cabin with an open bench that seats a family and heats to 194 degrees on an electric or wood burning heater, sold separately. Knotty cedar is $17,495 and clear cedar is available. Compared with the Serenity Mini you get the larger cabin for a household that saunas together after a day on the Bay.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-essential-bath: Ice fishers who spend February on Lake Simcoe already know cold, and the Chill Tub Essential Bath is the simplest way to bring that routine home: a bath format tub for a short daily plunge that does not need a dedicated room. Pricing is at the showroom, and it is on the floor on Bryne Drive so you can sit in it before you decide. It pairs with a Serenity sauna on a rural lot.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-essential-pod: A townhome garage in Ardagh Bluffs has room for the Essential Pod, the pod format of the Chill Tubs Essential line, which suits anyone who wants a daily plunge without giving up the whole parking spot. It plugs in like a small appliance and works as the cold half of a routine with a Clearlight cabin in the basement. Pricing is at the showroom, and both Essential models sit side by side on our floor so you can compare them.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-obsidian: Trail runners and cyclists around Blue Mountain in Collingwood use the Obsidian as their daily recovery step, a chilled and filtered Chill Tubs model that holds temperature for a routine rather than a novelty. Showroom pricing applies, and the team on Bryne Drive can walk you through how it differs from the Pro. Set it beside a Serenity cedar sauna outside a chalet and the contrast routine is done before dinner.
productBlurbs.chill-tub-pro: Open water swimmers who train off the beach in Wasaga want a cold plunge that keeps up with daily use in a hot July, and the Chill Tub Pro is the top of the Chill Tubs range for exactly that: active chilling and filtration built for a routine. Pricing is at the showroom, where it is set up and running next to the Obsidian. Pair it with a Clearlight cabin and you have the full contrast set up in a bungalow garage.
productBlurbs.summit-ws190: Ninety minutes on Highway 400 each way does a number on a lower back, and the Summit WS190 is the Wellness Shop massage chair we point commuters to when they want a full session at home rather than a monthly appointment. Pricing is at the showroom, and the chair is on the floor on Bryne Drive plugged in and ready, so sit in it for ten minutes before you decide. It is the step up from the Dreamcatcher WS170.
productBlurbs.dreamcatcher-ws170: Retirees in Orillia who drive down to Barrie for errands often stop in to try the Dreamcatcher WS170, the more accessible of our two Wellness Shop massage chairs, and a lot of them go home with one. Showroom pricing applies, and a chair is easier to judge in person than on a spec sheet, so bring whoever will use it most and let them sit. It suits a living room where a daily session is the goal.
productBlurbs.duke-series: The snow belt around Midland is where an enclosed Visscher Duke Series veranda earns its place, keeping a hot tub usable through a Georgian Bay squall and keeping the cover free of drifts. Western red cedar stands up to the damp, and multiple sizes let you match a J-285 or a Serenity sauna beside it. Pricing is at the showroom, where you can see the enclosed design and talk through footings for a waterfront lot.
productBlurbs.cypress-series: Innisfil subdivision yards back onto the neighbour's yard, and the Cypress Series cedar panel design from Visscher gives a hot tub privacy without the full enclosure of the Duke Series. Western red cedar can be left natural or stained, and multiple sizes cover a Jacuzzi or a Nordic round. Showroom pricing applies; ask us to price it with the tub so delivery happens on one day.
productBlurbs.hudson-series: Wind on an Oro-Medonte concession road has nothing to stop it, and the enclosed Hudson Series from Visscher at 11 by 14 feet and up puts walls around the tub so a January soak is not a January gale. Western red cedar, room for a seven seat Jacuzzi and the steps, and a door that keeps the snowbank outside. Pricing is at the showroom; bring your lot photos and we will talk about a base above the spring melt.
productBlurbs.sequoia-11-14: Sandy, flat lots in Wasaga Beach get full sun all afternoon, and the Sequoia 11 by 14 louvered gazebo from Visscher lets you open the roof for the sun and close it when the lake breeze turns. Open air design in western red cedar, sized for a full size hot tub with walking room around it. Showroom pricing applies, and the team on Bryne Drive can show you how the louvres work.
productBlurbs.sedona-9-9: Bradford's compact subdivision yards do not have space to waste, and the 9 by 9 Sedona is the smallest open air Visscher gazebo we carry, sized to cover a five or six seat tub and not much else. Western red cedar, an open design that suits a tub set against the house, and a footprint that leaves room for the barbecue. Pricing is at the showroom.
productBlurbs.savannah-11-11: Older Alliston homes have generous yards, and the 11 by 11 Savannah from Visscher sits over a seven seater like a Wellness Shop Ontario S104 with room to move around it under the roof. Open air in western red cedar, it gives shade in July and keeps the worst of the snow off a cover in January. Showroom pricing applies; the Sedona 9 by 9 is the smaller alternative for a tighter lot.

ui.salebarText: Red Tag 20% off every new 2026 Jacuzzi on the Barrie floor until
ui.heroTail: Come see every model running on Bryne Drive, one exit off Highway 400 at Mapleview, on your way to or from the cottage.
ui.hotTubsIntro: These are the tubs Simcoe County families ask for most, from plug and play rounds for the cottage to seven seaters for the subdivision, each with the same price online as at the counter.
ui.finderIntro: Four quick questions sort out seats, lounger or open seating, budget and whether the tub is headed for a Barrie backyard or a cottage with a 100 amp panel.
ui.swimHomeIntro: From a 12 foot family pool to a 19 foot training lane, every swim spa here runs through a Simcoe County winter, with pricing from $59 bi-weekly OAC.
ui.saunaHomeIntro: Clearlight infrared cabins from $10,495 fit a basement or condo and plug in; Serenity cedar outdoor saunas from $14,995 belong beside a snowbank on a rural lot or at the lake.

visitSteps.title: Sit in it heated
visitSteps.text: A spec sheet cannot tell you if the lounger fits your legs. Every tub on Bryne Drive is at temperature, so bring a swimsuit and find out.

visitSteps.title: Get a real delivery answer
visitSteps.text: Show us a photo of your gate, side yard and panel and our team will tell you dolly or crane, and roughly what the electrical run costs, before you commit.

visitSteps.title: Floor pricing you cannot click
visitSteps.text: Floor models, bundles and cottage delivery packages are quoted at the counter only, and they change as stock moves through the showroom.

brandBlurbs.Jacuzzi: Jacuzzi has built hot tubs since 1956, and on a Georgian Bay lot that record matters when the tub must run through thirty winters. PowerPro jets, CLEARRAY UV-C water care and the SmartTub app that heats it from the car.
brandBlurbs.Nordic: Round, tough and plug and play, Nordic tubs are made in Michigan and run on 110V, which is why so many go up Highway 11 to cottages with a 100 amp panel.
brandBlurbs.Wellness Shop: Our Ontario series is built in the USA with two 6 HP pumps and Thermal Shield insulation, the combination a Simcoe County snow belt winter demands, at a price well under a Jacuzzi.
brandBlurbs.Aquasolus: Built in Europe by Superior Wellness, Aquasolus puts a full size 6 or 7 seat tub in a Bradford or Innisfil new build from $10,995, with White Glove setup included.
brandBlurbs.SwimLife: SwimExpert and SwimFit swim spas give Lake Simcoe swimmers a lane from October to June, with ClearStream mineral water care and dual temperature options for the skiers in the house.
brandBlurbs.Clearlight: Full spectrum infrared cabins in Basswood or Mahogany with True Wave heaters, backed by a lifetime warranty on cabin and heaters, for commuters and shift workers who need daily recovery in the basement.
brandBlurbs.Serenity: Canadian made cedar outdoor saunas in knotty or clear cedar, ready for an electric heater in a Barrie yard or a wood burning one at a cottage where hydro is scarce.

ui.specialsIntro: These offers are written at the counter on Bryne Drive and change as stock moves; the Red Tag Jacuzzi clearance is the headline, and the rest are floor models and bundles.

claimSteps.title: Claim it online
claimSteps.text: Enter your name and mobile and a Red Tag voucher with its own code lands on your phone right away, with a seven day window.

claimSteps.title: We set it aside
claimSteps.text: Your voucher is logged at the Barrie showroom under your name, so the Red Tag price is waiting whether you come Tuesday or Saturday.

claimSteps.title: Show it at the counter
claimSteps.text: Bring the voucher on your phone or printed, and the team applies the 20% to your quote on any new 2026 Jacuzzi still in stock.

financingFaq.q: What does 0% for 12 months OAC actually mean for me?
financingFaq.a: On approved credit, you make bi-weekly payments for the first year with no interest charged. After that the balance continues on the amortization set for your product, and longer terms at regular rates are available if you want a lower payment. Approval depends on your credit file, and most answers come back within minutes.

financingFaq.q: Where do the bi-weekly numbers on the product pages come from?
financingFaq.a: Each one is the advertised starting payment for that model at its current sale price under the 0% for 12 months promotion, on approved credit. Amortization differs by product, so two tubs at similar prices can show different payments. The showroom can adjust the term and frequency to fit your budget.

financingFaq.q: Can the crane, cover lifter and chemicals go on the same financing?
financingFaq.a: Yes. Delivery, crane lifts for a cottage lot, covers, lifters, steps, start-up chemicals and showroom bundles can all roll into one bi-weekly payment. The one exception is the electrical hookup, which your licensed electrician invoices directly.

Usually not on approved credit. Most Barrie customers finance the whole purchase with nothing up front. If you would rather put some down to shorten the term or lower the payment, the team at Bryne Drive can run both scenarios for you.

buyCanadian.heading: Buy Canadian. Buy From Barrie.
buyCanadian.lead: The Wellness Shop grew from one local hot tub store into eight Ontario showrooms over 25 years. Buying in Barrie keeps the sale, the delivery crew and the service technician in Simcoe County.
points: An Ontario company for 25 years, with the Bryne Drive showroom staffed by people who live in Simcoe County.
Delivery crews and service technicians who work out of Barrie, from Alliston to Orillia and Collingwood.
Serenity outdoor saunas built in Canada from Western red cedar, set up beside the Jacuzzi floor models.
buyCanadian.pageLead: Buy Canadian does not mean a smaller tub. It means the company is headquartered in Ontario, the crew that gets the tub up a cottage road lives in Barrie, and the technician who answers a call in February starts the day on Bryne Drive.
body: The Wellness Shop began as a single local hot tub store and, 25 years later, runs eight showrooms across Ontario. Barrie covers Simcoe County and cottage country, from Innisfil to Midland and over to Collingwood, with staff who drive the 400 in the same snow you do. The sale, the delivery and the warranty work stay in the province.

We carry the names buyers come in for. As an authorized Jacuzzi dealer, every tub we sell carries the full factory warranty. Serenity saunas are built in Canada from Western red cedar. Our Wellness Shop Ontario series was specified for winters north of the city, with full foam insulation and covers that carry a real snow load. Buy Canadian here means the money and the service stay close, whichever badge is on the cabinet.
It shows most a few winters in, when a heater needs a look or a cover needs replacing. All of that runs through the Barrie showroom, with parts on the shelf and a crew that already knows your road.

faq.q: Is the Wellness Shop a Canadian company?
faq.a: Yes. The Wellness Shop is an Ontario company that grew from one local hot tub store into eight showrooms across the province, including the Barrie showroom on Bryne Drive. Sales, delivery and service are all handled by Ontario staff.

faq.q: Which products are made in Canada?
faq.a: Serenity outdoor saunas are built in Canada from Western red cedar. Jacuzzi hot tubs and our Wellness Shop Ontario series are built in the United States, Nordic tubs in Michigan and Aquasolus in Europe. Every one is sold by a Canadian company and delivered and serviced by the Barrie team.
